plantar-metatarsal-veins.summary: Veins that drain the toes and metatarsal spaces on the sole side. They flow into the plantar venous arch.
plantar-metatarsal-veins.clinical: These deep veins act as part of the foot pump during walking.
plantar-metatarsal-veins.course: Run backward along the metatarsal spaces in the sole.

plantar-venous-arch.name: Plantar Venous Arch
plantar-venous-arch.summary: A deep venous arch in the sole. It collects blood from the toes and forms the plantar veins.
plantar-venous-arch.clinical: Its blood is squeezed upward by foot movement, a mechanism called the foot pump.
plantar-venous-arch.course: Lies in the sole at the bases of the metatarsals, beside the plantar arterial arch.

popliteal-artery.name: Popliteal Artery
popliteal-artery.summary: The continuation of the femoral artery behind the knee. It is the deepest structure in the popliteal fossa.
popliteal-artery.clinical: Knee dislocation or a low femur fracture can tear it. Popliteal aneurysms are common.
popliteal-artery.course: Runs through the popliteal fossa to the lower border of popliteus, where it divides.
supplies: Rest of the leg (via its terminal branches)

popliteal-vein.name: Popliteal Vein
popliteal-vein.summary: The deep vein behind the knee. It is formed by the anterior and posterior tibial veins.
popliteal-vein.clinical: It is a common site of deep vein thrombosis, which causes calf swelling and pain.
popliteal-vein.course: Ascends through the popliteal fossa behind the artery and in front of the tibial nerve.

posterior-tibial-artery.name: Posterior Tibial Artery
posterior-tibial-artery.summary: The larger terminal branch of the popliteal artery. It supplies the back of the leg and the sole of the foot.
posterior-tibial-artery.clinical: Its pulse is felt behind the medial malleolus. It can be compressed in tarsal tunnel syndrome.
posterior-tibial-artery.from: Popliteal artery (at the lower border of popliteus)
posterior-tibial-artery.course: Descends deep to soleus, then passes behind the medial malleolus and splits into the plantar arteries.
supplies: Sole of the foot (via plantar arteries)

posterior-tibial-veins.name: Posterior Tibial Veins
posterior-tibial-veins.summary: Paired deep veins that accompany the posterior tibial artery. They drain the back of the leg and the sole.
posterior-tibial-veins.clinical: Calf deep vein thrombosis often involves these veins.
posterior-tibial-veins.into: Popliteal vein (with the anterior tibial veins)
posterior-tibial-veins.course: Ascend with the artery behind the medial malleolus, then deep to soleus.

small-saphenous-vein.name: Small Saphenous Vein
small-saphenous-vein.group: Superficial veins of the lower limb
small-saphenous-vein.summary: A superficial vein of the back of the leg. It starts at the lateral foot and drains into the popliteal vein.
small-saphenous-vein.clinical: It can become varicose. The sural nerve lies close to it, so it can be injured during vein surgery.
small-saphenous-vein.course: Starts behind the lateral malleolus, ascends along the back of the calf, and pierces the deep fascia.

superficial-branch-of-medial-plantar-art.name: Superficial Branch of Medial Plantar Artery
superficial-branch-of-medial-plantar-art.summary: A branch of the medial plantar artery. It supplies the skin of the inner sole.
superficial-branch-of-medial-plantar-art.clinical: It is a small vessel but important for healing of the skin of the sole.
superficial-branch-of-medial-plantar-art.course: Runs between the abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis toward the medial sole.
supplies: Medial side of the great toe

superficial-dorsal-veins-of-penis.name: Superficial Dorsal Veins of Penis
superficial-dorsal-veins-of-penis.summary: Veins that drain the skin of the penis. They run in the loose tissue under the skin.
superficial-dorsal-veins-of-penis.clinical: They can develop thrombophlebitis, known as penile Mondor disease.
superficial-dorsal-veins-of-penis.into: External pudendal veins, then the great saphenous vein
superficial-dorsal-veins-of-penis.course: Run along the top of the penis in the superficial fascia and pass to the groin.

superficial-external-pudendal-artery.name: Superficial External Pudendal Artery
superficial-external-pudendal-artery.summary: A small branch of the femoral artery. It supplies the skin of the lower abdomen and external genitalia.
superficial-external-pudendal-artery.clinical: It is a landmark vessel near the saphenous opening in groin surgery.
superficial-external-pudendal-artery.course: Passes medially over the groin, near the spermatic cord or round ligament.
supplies: Skin of the penis and scrotum or labia

right-subcostal-vein.name: Right Subcostal Vein
right-subcostal-vein.summary: The right subcostal vein runs below the 12th rib with the subcostal artery and nerve. It drains the upper posterior abdominal wall into the azygos vein.
right-subcostal-vein.clinical: It is one link between the azygos system and the lumbar veins, so it can carry blood around a blocked inferior vena cava.
drains: Posterior and lateral abdominal wall below the 12th rib
Skin and muscles of the flank
right-subcostal-vein.course: It runs below the 12th rib and passes behind the diaphragm. It unites with the right ascending lumbar vein to form the azygos vein.

spinal-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.name: Spinal Branch of Iliolumbar Artery
spinal-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.summary: This small branch of the iliolumbar artery enters the vertebral canal through the intervertebral foramen between L5 and the sacrum.
spinal-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.clinical: It joins the spinal arterial network that feeds the cauda equina and lower lumbar nerve roots.
spinal-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.from: Lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery
spinal-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.course: It passes medially through the foramen between L5 and S1 into the vertebral canal.
branches: Small twigs to the cauda equina and its coverings
supplies: Meninges of the lower vertebral canal

splenic-artery.name: Splenic Artery
splenic-artery.summary: The splenic artery is the largest branch of the celiac trunk. It runs a tortuous course along the upper border of the pancreas to the spleen.
splenic-artery.clinical: A splenic artery aneurysm can rupture, especially in pregnancy. A posterior gastric ulcer can erode into the artery and bleed heavily.
splenic-artery.course: It runs left behind the stomach along the upper border of the pancreas, then through the splenorenal ligament to the splenic hilum.
branches: Pancreatic branches (including dorsal pancreatic and great pancreatic arteries)
supplies: Body and tail of the pancreas
Fundus and greater curvature of the stomach

splenic-vein.name: Splenic Vein
splenic-vein.summary: The splenic vein collects blood from the spleen, pancreas, and part of the stomach. It joins the superior mesenteric vein to form the hepatic portal vein.
splenic-vein.clinical: Splenic vein thrombosis, often from pancreatitis, causes isolated gastric varices and an enlarged spleen (left-sided portal hypertension).
drains: Body and tail of the pancreas
Stomach (short gastric and left gastro-omental veins)
splenic-vein.course: It forms at the splenic hilum and runs right along the back of the pancreas, below the splenic artery. It joins the superior mesenteric vein behind the pancreatic neck.

subcostal-artery.name: Subcostal Artery
subcostal-artery.summary: The subcostal artery is the lowest paired branch of the thoracic aorta. It runs along the lower border of the 12th rib, below the last intercostal space.
subcostal-artery.clinical: It is the posterior intercostal artery of the 12th level and can be injured during flank incisions or kidney surgery.
subcostal-artery.course: It runs with the subcostal nerve and vein behind the lateral arcuate ligament, then lies between the abdominal wall muscles.
branches: Dorsal branch to the back muscles and spinal cord
Branches to the abdominal wall muscles
supplies: Muscles and skin of the upper posterior and lateral abdominal wall
Spinal cord and its coverings (via the dorsal branch)

superior-epigastric-artery.name: Superior Epigastric Artery
superior-epigastric-artery.summary: The superior epigastric artery is a terminal branch of the internal thoracic artery. It descends inside the rectus sheath behind the rectus abdominis muscle.
superior-epigastric-artery.clinical: It joins the inferior epigastric artery, giving a collateral route between the subclavian and external iliac arteries when the aorta is narrowed.
superior-epigastric-artery.course: It enters the rectus sheath between the sternal and costal parts of the diaphragm. It descends behind rectus abdominis and meets the inferior epigastric artery.
branches: Small branches to the diaphragm and falciform ligament

superior-epigastric-veins.name: Superior Epigastric Veins
superior-epigastric-veins.summary: The superior epigastric veins accompany the superior epigastric artery. They drain the upper anterior abdominal wall into the internal thoracic veins.
superior-epigastric-veins.clinical: They connect with the inferior epigastric veins, forming a deep route between the superior and inferior vena cava systems.
superior-epigastric-veins.into: Internal thoracic veins (then the brachiocephalic vein)
superior-epigastric-veins.course: They run as paired companion veins behind rectus abdominis, within the rectus sheath, and anastomose with the inferior epigastric veins.

superior-mesenteric-artery.name: Superior Mesenteric Artery
superior-mesenteric-artery.group: Unpaired branches of the abdominal aorta
superior-mesenteric-artery.summary: The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut. It arises from the aorta at L1 and runs down in the root of the mesentery.
superior-mesenteric-artery.clinical: Embolism or thrombosis causes acute mesenteric ischemia, with severe pain out of proportion to the exam. It can also compress the duodenum (SMA syndrome).
superior-mesenteric-artery.course: It passes behind the pancreatic neck, then in front of the uncinate process and third part of the duodenum. It descends in the mesentery root toward the right iliac fossa.
supplies: Lower duodenum and head of the pancreas
Proximal two thirds of the transverse colon

superior-mesenteric-vein.name: Superior Mesenteric Vein
superior-mesenteric-vein.summary: The superior mesenteric vein drains the midgut. It lies to the right of the superior mesenteric artery and joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.
superior-mesenteric-vein.clinical: Superior mesenteric vein thrombosis causes bowel ischemia. The vein is also a landmark when judging whether a pancreatic head tumor can be removed.
drains: Head of the pancreas and lower duodenum
superior-mesenteric-vein.course: It begins in the right iliac fossa and ascends in the mesentery root, right of its artery. It passes in front of the uncinate process and joins the splenic vein behind the pancreatic neck.

superior-lateral-genicular-artery.name: Superior Lateral Genicular Artery
superior-lateral-genicular-artery.summary: This branch of the popliteal artery curves around the femur just above the lateral femoral condyle. It helps supply the knee joint.
superior-lateral-genicular-artery.clinical: It can be injured during lateral release or lateral knee approaches. Embolizing the genicular arteries is a treatment for painful knee osteoarthritis.
superior-lateral-genicular-artery.course: It passes laterally above the lateral femoral condyle, deep to the biceps femoris tendon, and divides into superficial and deep branches.
supplies: Lateral side of the knee joint capsule and patella

superior-medial-genicular-artery.name: Superior Medial Genicular Artery
superior-medial-genicular-artery.summary: This branch of the popliteal artery curves around the femur just above the medial femoral condyle. It forms part of the arterial network around the knee.
superior-medial-genicular-artery.clinical: Genicular artery embolization targets this vessel and its neighbors to relieve knee osteoarthritis pain. It may also be injured in medial knee surgery.
superior-medial-genicular-artery.course: It passes medially above the medial femoral condyle, deep to the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons and in front of the adductor magnus tendon.
supplies: Medial side of the knee joint capsule

superior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.name: Superior Basal Vein of Right Lung
superior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.summary: The superior basal vein drains part of the basal segments of the right lower lobe. It joins the inferior basal vein to form the common basal vein.
superior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood. Resection of a lower lobe segment requires careful division of these segmental veins.
drains: Basal segments of the right lower lobe (mainly anterior and lateral basal)
superior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.into: Common basal vein, then the right inferior pulmonary vein
superior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.course: It runs between lung segments toward the hilum and merges with the inferior basal vein behind the hilum.

superior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.name: Superior Lingular Artery of Left Lung
superior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.summary: This segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery supplies the superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe. The lingula is the left lung counterpart of the right middle lobe.
superior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-poor blood. A pulmonary embolus lodged here blocks blood flow to the superior lingular segment.
superior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.from: Left pulmonary artery (lingular branch of the superior lobar artery)
superior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.course: It descends beside the lingular bronchus into the superior lingular segment of the upper lobe.
supplies: Superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe

superior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.name: Superior Lingular Vein of Left Lung
superior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.summary: This vein drains the superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe. It joins the inferior lingular vein to form the lingular vein.
superior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. Variation in their branching matters in left upper lobe surgery.
drains: Superior lingular segment of the left upper lobe
superior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.course: It runs in the plane between lung segments toward the hilum and joins the left superior pulmonary vein.

superior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.name: Superior Lobar Artery of Right Lung
superior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.latin: Arteria lobaris superior pulmonis dextri (truncus anterior)
superior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.summary: This is the first branch of the right pulmonary artery. It supplies the right upper lobe and usually arises just before the artery enters the lung.
superior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: A saddle or lobar pulmonary embolus can block this artery. It lies in front of the right upper lobe bronchus, which helps surgeons identify it.
superior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.course: It arises outside the hilum, in front of the right main bronchus, and enters the upper lobe.
supplies: Right upper lobe of the lung

superior-phrenic-arteries.name: Superior Phrenic Arteries
superior-phrenic-arteries.summary: These small paired arteries arise from the lowest thoracic aorta near the aortic hiatus. They supply the upper back surface of the diaphragm.
superior-phrenic-arteries.clinical: They are small and rarely matter alone. They help link the diaphragm to the musculophrenic and pericardiacophrenic arteries.
superior-phrenic-arteries.course: They run a short distance onto the upper surface of the posterior part of the diaphragm.
branches: Small branches that anastomose with the musculophrenic and pericardiacophrenic arteries
supplies: Posterior part of the diaphragm (upper surface)

superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.name: Superior Segmental Artery of Left Lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.parent: Inferior lobar artery of left lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.summary: This branch of the left inferior lobar artery supplies the superior segment of the left lower lobe.
superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.clinical: The superior segment is a common site for aspiration pneumonia and lung abscess in patients who lie on their backs.
superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.from: Inferior lobar artery of the left lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.course: It is usually the first branch of the lower lobe artery and runs backward with the superior segmental bronchus.
supplies: Superior segment of the left lower lobe

superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.name: Superior Segmental Artery of Right Lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.parent: Inferior lobar artery of right lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.summary: This branch of the right inferior lobar artery supplies the superior segment of the right lower lobe.
superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: Aspiration often lodges in this segment in patients lying on their backs, so abscesses form here.
superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.from: Inferior lobar artery of the right lung
superior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.course: It is usually the first branch of the lower lobe artery and runs backward with the superior segmental bronchus.
supplies: Superior segment of the right lower lobe

superior-vein-of-left-lung.name: Superior Vein of Left Lung
superior-vein-of-left-lung.latin: Vena superior lobi inferioris pulmonis sinistri
superior-vein-of-left-lung.summary: This vein drains the superior segment of the left lower lobe. It joins the common basal vein to form the left inferior pulmonary vein.
superior-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. Segmental veins are tied off in lower lobe resections.
drains: Superior segment of the left lower lobe
superior-vein-of-left-lung.course: It runs through the lower lobe toward the hilum and joins the common basal vein behind the hilum.

superior-vein-of-right-lung.name: Superior Vein of Right Lung
superior-vein-of-right-lung.latin: Vena superior lobi inferioris pulmonis dextri
superior-vein-of-right-lung.summary: This vein drains the superior segment of the right lower lobe. It joins the common basal vein to form the right inferior pulmonary vein.
superior-vein-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium. Segmental veins are tied off in lower lobe resections.
drains: Superior segment of the right lower lobe
superior-vein-of-right-lung.course: It runs through the lower lobe toward the hilum and joins the common basal vein behind the hilum.

superior-vena-cava.name: Superior Vena Cava
superior-vena-cava.summary: The superior vena cava returns blood from the head, neck, upper limbs, and chest wall to the right atrium. It is about 7 cm long and has no valves.
superior-vena-cava.clinical: Tumors or clots can compress it, causing SVC syndrome with facial swelling and distended neck veins. Central venous lines often end here.
superior-vena-cava.course: It forms behind the first right costal cartilage where the brachiocephalic veins unite. It descends on the right of the ascending aorta, receives the azygos vein, and enters the right atrium.

supreme-intercostal-artery.name: Supreme Intercostal Artery
supreme-intercostal-artery.summary: The supreme intercostal artery descends over the neck of the first rib. It supplies the first and second posterior intercostal spaces.
supreme-intercostal-artery.clinical: A lung apex (Pancoast) tumor can invade this region along with the sympathetic chain and the lower brachial plexus.
supreme-intercostal-artery.course: It descends behind the cervical pleura, in front of the necks of the first and second ribs.
supplies: Adjacent back muscles and spinal cord coverings

thoracic-aorta.name: Thoracic Aorta
thoracic-aorta.summary: The thoracic aorta continues from the aortic arch at the lower border of T4. It descends in the posterior mediastinum to the aortic hiatus at T12.
thoracic-aorta.clinical: Aortic dissection and traumatic rupture can occur here, often just beyond the origin of the left subclavian artery (the isthmus).
thoracic-aorta.course: It begins left of the vertebral column, moves toward the midline as it descends, and passes behind the diaphragm at T12.

thyrocervical-trunk.name: Thyrocervical Trunk
thyrocervical-trunk.summary: This short trunk arises from the first part of the subclavian artery near the medial edge of anterior scalene. It splits into three arteries.
thyrocervical-trunk.clinical: The inferior thyroid artery lies close to the recurrent laryngeal nerve, so thyroid surgeons must take care when tying it.
thyrocervical-trunk.course: It rises a short distance before dividing at the medial border of the anterior scalene muscle.
supplies: Muscles of the neck and upper back

transverse-cervical-artery.name: Transverse Cervical Artery
transverse-cervical-artery.summary: The transverse cervical artery crosses the posterior triangle of the neck above the clavicle. It supplies the trapezius and nearby back muscles.
transverse-cervical-artery.clinical: It can be cut in neck dissections. Surgeons also use it as a recipient vessel for free tissue transfer.
transverse-cervical-artery.course: It crosses the anterior scalene muscle and phrenic nerve, runs across the posterior triangle, and passes deep to the trapezius.
branches: Deep branch to the rhomboid muscles (dorsal scapular artery in some people)

anterior-division-of-internal-iliac-arte.name: Anterior Division of Internal Iliac Artery
anterior-division-of-internal-iliac-arte.summary: The anterior division is the larger part of the internal iliac artery. It supplies the pelvic organs, the perineum, and part of the buttock and medial thigh.
anterior-division-of-internal-iliac-arte.clinical: Branches of this division are the targets when surgeons ligate or embolize the internal iliac artery to control pelvic bleeding.
anterior-division-of-internal-iliac-arte.course: It runs forward and down along the lateral pelvic wall, giving off visceral and parietal branches.
branches: Inferior vesical artery (vaginal artery in females)
supplies: Bladder, rectum, and prostate or uterus and vagina

common-iliac-artery.name: Common Iliac Artery
common-iliac-artery.summary: The two common iliac arteries are the terminal branches of the abdominal aorta. Each divides into internal and external iliac arteries near the sacroiliac joint.
common-iliac-artery.clinical: Blockage of the aortic bifurcation and common iliac arteries causes Leriche syndrome, with buttock pain and erectile dysfunction. The right artery can compress the left common iliac vein.
common-iliac-artery.course: Each runs down and outward along the medial edge of psoas major for about 5 cm. The right artery is longer and crosses in front of the left common iliac vein.
supplies: Pelvis and lower limb (through its two branches)

common-iliac-vein.name: Common Iliac Vein
common-iliac-vein.group: Tributaries of the inferior vena cava
common-iliac-vein.summary: The common iliac vein is formed by the external and internal iliac veins. The two common iliac veins unite at L5 to form the inferior vena cava.
common-iliac-vein.clinical: The left vein passes behind the right common iliac artery and can be compressed there (May-Thurner syndrome), raising the risk of left leg clots.
common-iliac-vein.course: Each vein ascends obliquely beside its artery. The left vein is longer and crosses behind the right common iliac artery to join the right vein.

common-plantar-digital-arteries.name: Common Plantar Digital Arteries
common-plantar-digital-arteries.summary: These short arteries continue the plantar metatarsal arteries toward the toes. Each one splits into two proper plantar digital arteries.
common-plantar-digital-arteries.clinical: They are small vessels that matter in foot ischemia and in diabetic toe wounds.
common-plantar-digital-arteries.course: Each runs forward in the sole between the heads of the metatarsals to the web space between two toes, where it divides.
supplies: Plantar side of the toes (through the proper digital arteries)

deep-artery-of-penis.name: Deep Artery of Penis
deep-artery-of-penis.summary: The deep artery of the penis runs inside each corpus cavernosum. It fills the erectile tissue with blood during erection.
deep-artery-of-penis.clinical: Damage to this artery or its helicine branches, from trauma or atherosclerosis, is a cause of erectile dysfunction.
deep-artery-of-penis.course: It pierces the crus of the penis and runs along the center of the corpus cavernosum.
supplies: Corpus cavernosum of the penis (erectile tissue)

deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis.name: Deep Dorsal Vein of Penis
deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis.summary: The deep dorsal vein is the main vein of the penis. It lies in the midline under the deep fascia, between the two dorsal arteries.
deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis.clinical: It is part of the dorsal venous complex, which surgeons tie off in radical prostatectomy to control bleeding. Compressing it helps maintain an erection.
drains: Corpora cavernosa and spongiosum (through circumflex veins)
deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis.into: Prostatic venous plexus, then the internal iliac veins
deep-dorsal-vein-of-penis.course: It runs back along the dorsum of the penis. It passes under the pubic symphysis, between the arcuate pubic and transverse perineal ligaments, to the prostatic plexus.

dorsal-artery-of-penis.name: Dorsal Artery of Penis
dorsal-artery-of-penis.summary: The dorsal artery of the penis runs along the upper surface of the penis, deep to the deep fascia. It lies beside the deep dorsal vein and dorsal nerve.
dorsal-artery-of-penis.clinical: Its supply to the glans is important in penile surgery and trauma.
dorsal-artery-of-penis.course: It passes between the crus and the pubic symphysis, then runs forward on the dorsum of the penis to the glans.
supplies: Skin and fascia of the penis

dorsal-digital-arteries-of-foot.name: Dorsal Digital Arteries of Foot
dorsal-digital-arteries-of-foot.summary: These small arteries run along the sides of the toes on the dorsum of the foot. They supply the top of the toes.
dorsal-digital-arteries-of-foot.clinical: They are fine end vessels and are often the first to fail in peripheral artery disease, causing cold toes.
dorsal-digital-arteries-of-foot.course: Each dorsal metatarsal artery divides near the toe web into two dorsal digital arteries for the sides of neighboring toes.
supplies: Skin on the dorsal surface of the toes, mainly the proximal parts

external-iliac-artery.name: External Iliac Artery
external-iliac-artery.summary: The external iliac artery carries blood from the pelvis to the lower limb. It becomes the femoral artery at the inguinal ligament.
external-iliac-artery.clinical: Atherosclerosis here causes leg claudication. In some cyclists, kinking and endofibrosis narrows the artery.
external-iliac-artery.course: It runs along the medial border of psoas major and the pelvic brim. It ends at the inguinal ligament, midway between the pubic symphysis and the anterior superior iliac spine.

external-iliac-vein.name: External Iliac Vein
external-iliac-vein.summary: The external iliac vein carries blood from the lower limb to the pelvis. It begins at the inguinal ligament as the continuation of the femoral vein.
external-iliac-vein.clinical: Clots in the iliofemoral veins can cause marked swelling of the whole leg and carry a high risk of pulmonary embolism.
external-iliac-vein.into: Common iliac vein (after joining the internal iliac vein)
external-iliac-vein.course: It runs up along the pelvic brim, medial to its artery, and joins the internal iliac vein in front of the sacroiliac joint. It receives the inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac veins.

iliacus-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.name: Iliacus Branch of Iliolumbar Artery
iliacus-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.summary: The iliac branch of the iliolumbar artery runs in the iliac fossa. It supplies the iliacus muscle and the iliac bone.
iliacus-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.clinical: It links with the deep circumflex iliac and obturator arteries, giving collateral flow around the pelvis.
iliacus-branch-of-iliolumbar-artery.course: It runs laterally on the iliacus muscle, sending a nutrient branch into the ilium and anastomosing along the iliac crest.

inferior-gluteal-artery.name: Inferior Gluteal Artery
inferior-gluteal-artery.summary: The inferior gluteal artery leaves the pelvis below piriformis. It supplies the buttock and the back of the upper thigh.
inferior-gluteal-artery.clinical: It supplies the sciatic nerve and joins the cruciate anastomosis, so it helps keep blood flow to the hip if other vessels are blocked.
inferior-gluteal-artery.from: Anterior division of the internal iliac artery
inferior-gluteal-artery.course: It exits through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, deep to gluteus maximus, with the inferior gluteal nerve.
branches: Anastomotic branches to the cruciate anastomosis

inferior-gluteal-veins.name: Inferior Gluteal Veins
inferior-gluteal-veins.summary: The inferior gluteal veins accompany the inferior gluteal artery. They drain the lower buttock and upper back of the thigh into the internal iliac vein.
inferior-gluteal-veins.clinical: They connect with the femoral system through the cruciate anastomosis, giving an alternative route if the femoral vein is blocked.
inferior-gluteal-veins.course: They pass through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis and run up into the pelvis to join the internal iliac vein.

intercapitular-veins-of-foot.name: Intercapitular Veins of Foot
intercapitular-veins-of-foot.group: Veins of the sole and toes
intercapitular-veins-of-foot.summary: These small veins pass between the heads of the metatarsals. They connect the plantar and dorsal venous systems of the foot.
intercapitular-veins-of-foot.clinical: They are the route by which blood from the sole drains up to the dorsal venous arch when the foot bears weight.
intercapitular-veins-of-foot.into: Dorsal metatarsal veins and the dorsal venous arch
intercapitular-veins-of-foot.course: Each vein runs through the interval between adjacent metatarsal heads to link the plantar veins with the dorsal veins.

internal-iliac-artery.name: Internal Iliac Artery
internal-iliac-artery.summary: The internal iliac artery is the main blood supply of the pelvis. It arises from the common iliac artery and divides into anterior and posterior divisions.
internal-iliac-artery.clinical: Surgeons ligate or embolize it to control severe pelvic or obstetric hemorrhage. Collateral flow usually keeps pelvic tissue alive.
internal-iliac-artery.from: Common iliac artery (at the pelvic brim)
internal-iliac-artery.course: It runs down and back for about 4 cm to the upper edge of the greater sciatic foramen, where it divides.

internal-iliac-vein.name: Internal Iliac Vein
internal-iliac-vein.summary: The internal iliac vein drains the pelvis, gluteal region, and perineum. It joins the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.
internal-iliac-vein.clinical: It connects to the vertebral venous plexus, so pelvic cancers can spread to the spine. Pelvic venous congestion can cause chronic pelvic pain.
internal-iliac-vein.course: It forms above the greater sciatic foramen and ascends behind and medial to its artery to the pelvic brim. Its tributaries match the arterial branches.

internal-pudendal-artery.name: Internal Pudendal Artery
internal-pudendal-artery.summary: The internal pudendal artery is the main artery of the perineum and external genitalia. It leaves the pelvis and re-enters through the lesser sciatic foramen.
internal-pudendal-artery.clinical: Injury or narrowing can cause erectile dysfunction. Compression in the pudendal canal contributes to pudendal neuralgia.
internal-pudendal-artery.from: Anterior division of the internal iliac artery
internal-pudendal-artery.course: It exits the pelvis below piriformis, hooks around the ischial spine, and runs forward in the pudendal canal with the pudendal nerve.
branches: Deep artery of the penis or clitoris
Dorsal artery of the penis or clitoris

internal-pudendal-vein.name: Internal Pudendal Vein
internal-pudendal-vein.summary: The internal pudendal veins accompany the internal pudendal artery. They drain the perineum and external genitalia into the internal iliac vein.
internal-pudendal-vein.clinical: These veins help drain the penis or clitoris after erection and are part of the venous routes in the pudendal canal.
drains: Lower anal canal (via inferior rectal veins)
internal-pudendal-vein.course: They run in the pudendal canal beside the artery, exit through the greater sciatic foramen, and enter the internal iliac vein.

lateral-sacral-veins.name: Lateral Sacral Veins
lateral-sacral-veins.summary: The lateral sacral veins accompany the lateral sacral arteries. They drain the sacral canal and the front of the sacrum into the internal iliac vein.
lateral-sacral-veins.clinical: Presacral veins connect to the vertebral venous plexus. Tearing them during rectal surgery can cause bleeding that is hard to control.
lateral-sacral-veins.course: They run on the front of the sacrum and link with the vertebral venous plexus through the sacral foramina. They drain upward into the internal iliac vein.

medial-circumflex-femoral-veins.name: Medial Circumflex Femoral Veins
medial-circumflex-femoral-veins.summary: These veins accompany the medial circumflex femoral artery. They drain the hip joint and the upper medial thigh into the femoral vein.
medial-circumflex-femoral-veins.clinical: The accompanying artery is the main supply of the femoral head, so hip surgery or femoral neck fracture can injure this region.
medial-circumflex-femoral-veins.course: They pass between pectineus and iliopsoas, then curve around the femoral neck toward the back of the thigh.

median-sacral-artery.name: Median Sacral Artery
median-sacral-artery.group: Unpaired branches of the abdominal aorta
median-sacral-artery.summary: The median sacral artery is a small midline branch of the aorta. It descends over the lower lumbar vertebrae, sacrum, and coccyx.
median-sacral-artery.clinical: It can bleed during surgery in front of the sacrum, such as rectal mobilization or sacral fixation.
median-sacral-artery.from: Back of the abdominal aorta, just above the bifurcation
median-sacral-artery.course: It descends in the midline in front of L4, L5, the sacrum, and the coccyx, behind the left common iliac vein.
branches: Branches that join the lateral sacral arteries

perforating-branches-of-plantar-metatars.name: Perforating Branches of Plantar Metatarsal Arteries
perforating-branches-of-plantar-metatars.summary: These small branches pass upward between the metatarsals. They connect the plantar metatarsal arteries with the dorsal metatarsal arteries.
perforating-branches-of-plantar-metatars.clinical: They let blood reach the top of the foot if the dorsalis pedis artery is blocked, and the reverse.
perforating-branches-of-plantar-metatars.course: They pass dorsally through the spaces between the metatarsal heads to join the dorsal metatarsal arteries.
branches: Junctions with the dorsal metatarsal arteries
supplies: Link between the plantar and dorsal arterial systems

plantar-digital-veins.name: Plantar Digital Veins
plantar-digital-veins.group: Veins of the sole and toes
plantar-digital-veins.summary: The plantar digital veins drain the underside of the toes. They run along the sides of each toe and feed the plantar metatarsal veins.
plantar-digital-veins.clinical: Blood from the toes mainly returns through the dorsal veins when standing, but these veins connect the two systems.
plantar-digital-veins.into: Plantar metatarsal veins, then the plantar venous arch
plantar-digital-veins.course: They run on each side of the toe, join the intercapitular veins, and form the plantar metatarsal veins.

posterior-division-of-internal-iliac-art.name: Posterior Division of Internal Iliac Artery
posterior-division-of-internal-iliac-art.summary: The posterior division is the smaller part of the internal iliac artery. It supplies the pelvic wall and the buttock.
posterior-division-of-internal-iliac-art.clinical: The superior gluteal artery, its largest branch, can be injured in fractures through the greater sciatic notch.
posterior-division-of-internal-iliac-art.course: It passes backward toward the greater sciatic foramen and gives off three parietal branches.

proper-plantar-digital-arteries.name: Proper Plantar Digital Arteries
proper-plantar-digital-arteries.summary: The proper plantar digital arteries run along the sides of the toes on the sole. They supply the toe pads and nail beds.
proper-plantar-digital-arteries.clinical: They are small end arteries. Injury to a pair can threaten a toe because collateral flow is limited.
proper-plantar-digital-arteries.course: Each common plantar digital artery divides into two proper digital arteries that run to opposite sides of the neighboring toes.
branches: Small branches to the toe pad and nail bed

right-testicular-artery-001.name: Left Testicular Artery
right-testicular-artery-001.group: Paired branches of the abdominal aorta
right-testicular-artery-001.summary: The testicular artery arises from the aorta below the renal arteries and runs to the testis.
right-testicular-artery-001.clinical: Surgeons try to preserve this artery in varicocele surgery and hernia repair, because it is the main blood supply of the testis.
right-testicular-artery-001.from: Abdominal aorta (just below the renal arteries, about L2)
right-testicular-artery-001.course: It runs down behind the peritoneum on psoas major, in front of the ureter, then enters the deep inguinal ring in the spermatic cord.

right-testicular-artery.name: Right Testicular Artery
right-testicular-artery.group: Paired branches of the abdominal aorta
right-testicular-artery.summary: The right testicular artery arises from the front of the aorta below the renal arteries. It runs to the testis and epididymis.
right-testicular-artery.clinical: Surgeons try to preserve this artery in varicocele surgery and hernia repair, because it is the main blood supply of the testis.
right-testicular-artery.from: Abdominal aorta (just below the renal arteries, about L2)
right-testicular-artery.course: It runs down behind the peritoneum on psoas major. It passes in front of the inferior vena cava and right ureter, then enters the deep inguinal ring.

right-testicular-vein.name: Right Testicular Vein
right-testicular-vein.group: Tributaries of the inferior vena cava
right-testicular-vein.summary: The right testicular vein drains the testis and epididymis. It empties directly into the inferior vena cava, just below the right renal vein.
right-testicular-vein.clinical: A new right-sided varicocele can signal a mass or clot in the inferior vena cava or retroperitoneum. Varicoceles are far more common on the left.
right-testicular-vein.into: Inferior vena cava (the left vein drains into the left renal vein)
right-testicular-vein.course: It forms from the pampiniform plexus in the spermatic cord, passes through the inguinal canal, and ascends in front of psoas major and the ureter.

sigmoid-arteries.name: Sigmoid Arteries
sigmoid-arteries.summary: The sigmoid arteries are two to four branches of the inferior mesenteric artery. They run in the sigmoid mesocolon to the sigmoid colon.
sigmoid-arteries.clinical: Small straight vessels from these arteries pierce the colon wall, and diverticula often form at those points. The watershed near the rectosigmoid junction is prone to ischemia.
sigmoid-arteries.course: They run down and to the left in the sigmoid mesocolon and divide into ascending and descending branches that form arcades.
branches: Ascending branch (joins the left colic artery)
Descending branch (joins the superior rectal artery)

sigmoid-veins.name: Sigmoid Veins
sigmoid-veins.summary: The sigmoid veins drain the sigmoid colon. They flow into the inferior mesenteric vein, which empties into the portal system.
sigmoid-veins.clinical: The inferior mesenteric vein links to the rectal veins, a portal-systemic connection that can swell into hemorrhoids in portal hypertension.
sigmoid-veins.course: They accompany the sigmoid arteries in the sigmoid mesocolon and join to form the inferior mesenteric vein.

superficial-epigastric-artery.name: Superficial Epigastric Artery
superficial-epigastric-artery.summary: The superficial epigastric artery arises from the femoral artery just below the inguinal ligament. It runs up over the ligament to the lower abdominal skin.
superficial-epigastric-artery.clinical: It is used as a source vessel in some breast reconstruction flaps, though it is often small or absent.
superficial-epigastric-artery.from: Femoral artery (about 1 cm below the inguinal ligament)
superficial-epigastric-artery.course: It pierces the fascia lata, crosses the inguinal ligament in the subcutaneous tissue, and runs toward the umbilicus.
supplies: Skin and superficial fascia of the lower anterior abdominal wall

superficial-epigastric-vein.name: Superficial Epigastric Vein
superficial-epigastric-vein.summary: The superficial epigastric vein drains the skin of the lower abdominal wall. It empties into the great saphenous vein near the saphenofemoral junction.
superficial-epigastric-vein.clinical: It can link to the thoracoepigastric vein, giving a superficial route between the vena cava systems if a cava is blocked.
drains: Skin and superficial fascia of the lower abdominal wall
superficial-epigastric-vein.course: It runs down over the inguinal ligament in the subcutaneous tissue and enters the great saphenous vein at the saphenous opening.

superior-gluteal-artery.name: Superior Gluteal Artery
superior-gluteal-artery.summary: The superior gluteal artery is the largest branch of the posterior division. It leaves the pelvis above piriformis to supply the gluteal muscles.
superior-gluteal-artery.clinical: It can be torn in pelvic or sciatic notch fractures. Surgeons also use it for the superior gluteal artery perforator flap.
superior-gluteal-artery.from: Posterior division of the internal iliac artery
superior-gluteal-artery.course: It passes between the lumbosacral trunk and S1 nerve, exits above piriformis with the superior gluteal nerve, and divides into superficial and deep branches.
branches: Deep branch (upper and lower divisions) to gluteus medius and minimus

superior-gluteal-vein.name: Superior Gluteal Vein
superior-gluteal-vein.summary: The superior gluteal veins accompany the superior gluteal artery. They drain the gluteal muscles into the internal iliac vein.
superior-gluteal-vein.clinical: These thin-walled veins can retract into the pelvis when torn in fractures, causing bleeding that is hard to control.
superior-gluteal-vein.course: They pass through the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis and enter the pelvis to join the internal iliac vein.

right-posterolateral-branch.name: Right Posterolateral Branch
right-posterolateral-branch.summary: The continuation of the right coronary artery beyond the crux of the heart. It supplies the back of the left ventricle.
right-posterolateral-branch.from: Right coronary artery, after it gives off the posterior interventricular artery at the crux
right-posterolateral-branch.course: Continues in the coronary sulcus onto the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle, running toward the left margin.
branches: Small branches to the posterior wall of the left ventricle
supplies: Posterior (inferior) wall of the left ventricle in right-dominant hearts
right-posterolateral-branch.clinical: Blockage can add to inferior or posterolateral wall infarction when the right coronary artery is the dominant vessel.

accessory-hemi-azygos-vein.name: Accessory Hemi-azygos Vein
accessory-hemi-azygos-vein.summary: A small vein on the left side of the upper thoracic vertebral column. It drains the upper left posterior intercostal spaces.
accessory-hemi-azygos-vein.into: Azygos vein at about T7 to T8 (sometimes the hemi-azygos vein)
accessory-hemi-azygos-vein.course: Descends on the left of the vertebral bodies, then crosses the midline behind the aorta, thoracic duct, and esophagus to join the azygos vein.
accessory-hemi-azygos-vein.clinical: It may connect above with the left superior intercostal vein. It forms part of a collateral route if the superior or inferior vena cava is blocked.

anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.name: Anterior Basal Segmental Artery of Left Lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.latin: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis sinistri
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.parent: Inferior lobar artery of left lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.summary: A segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery to segment S8. It carries deoxygenated blood to the anterior basal segment of the left lower lobe.
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.from: Basal trunk of the inferior lobar artery of the left lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the anterior basal segment of the left lower lobe
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-.clinical: Pulmonary embolism can block segmental arteries and cause a wedge-shaped infarct. On the left, the anterior and medial basal segments are often fused.

anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.name: Anterior Basal Segmental Artery of Right Lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.latin: Arteria segmentalis basalis anterior pulmonis dextri
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.parent: Inferior lobar artery of right lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.summary: A segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery to segment S8. It carries deoxygenated blood to the anterior basal segment of the right lower lobe.
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.from: Basal trunk of the inferior lobar artery of the right lung
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the anterior basal segment of the right lower lobe
anterior-basal-segmental-artery-of-right.clinical: A pulmonary embolus lodged in a segmental artery can cause a wedge-shaped infarct reaching the pleura, with pleuritic chest pain.

anterior-interventricular-artery-left-an.name: Anterior Interventricular Artery (Left Anterior Descending)
anterior-interventricular-artery-left-an.summary: The larger terminal branch of the left coronary artery. It runs down the front of the heart and supplies much of the left ventricle and septum.
anterior-interventricular-artery-left-an.from: Left coronary artery, when it divides behind the pulmonary trunk
anterior-interventricular-artery-left-an.course: Descends in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex. It often wraps around the apex to meet the posterior interventricular artery.
branches: Diagonal branches to the anterolateral left ventricle
supplies: Anterior wall of the left ventricle
Anterior two thirds of the interventricular septum
Right and left bundle branches (septal part)
anterior-interventricular-artery-left-an.clinical: Called the widowmaker. Blockage causes a large anterior wall infarct, and the left internal thoracic artery is the usual bypass graft to it.

anterior-jugular-vein.name: Anterior Jugular Vein
anterior-jugular-vein.summary: A small superficial vein that runs down the front of the neck near the midline. Its size varies greatly between people.
drains: Submental and superficial veins of the front of the neck
anterior-jugular-vein.into: External jugular vein or subclavian vein, just above the clavicle
anterior-jugular-vein.course: Begins near the hyoid bone and descends beside the midline. It turns laterally above the sternum, passes deep to sternocleidomastoid, and ends near the clavicle. The two sides often join across the midline by a jugular venous arch.
anterior-jugular-vein.clinical: The jugular venous arch lies in the suprasternal space and can bleed during a tracheostomy or neck incision.

anterior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.name: Anterior Papillary Muscle of Right Ventricle
anterior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.summary: The largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle. It anchors the tricuspid valve through its chordae tendineae.
anterior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.location: Rises from the anterior wall of the right ventricle. The moderator band usually joins its base.
function: Holds the anterior and posterior (inferior) tricuspid leaflets closed during systole through chordae tendineae
Prevents the leaflets from prolapsing into the right atrium
anterior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
anterior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.clinical: Rupture or dysfunction causes tricuspid regurgitation. The moderator band carries the right bundle branch to this muscle.

anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.name: Anterior Segmental Artery of Left Lung
anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.parent: Superior lobar artery of left lung
anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery to segment S3. It carries deoxygenated blood to the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.from: Superior lobar branches of the left pulmonary artery as it arches over the left main bronchus
anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the anterior segment of the left upper lobe
anterior-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.clinical: Segmental anatomy lets surgeons remove one segment by dividing its artery, bronchus, and vein. Emboli can block it and cause infarction.

anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.name: Anterior Segmental Artery of Right Lung
anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.parent: Superior lobar artery of right lung
anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery to segment S3. It carries deoxygenated blood to the anterior segment of the right upper lobe.
anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.from: Superior (anterior) trunk of the right pulmonary artery
anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the anterior segment of the right upper lobe
anterior-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: Segmental anatomy lets surgeons remove one segment by dividing its artery, bronchus, and vein. Emboli can block it and cause infarction.

anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.name: Anterior Semilunar Leaflet of Pulmonary Valve
anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.latin: Valvula semilunaris anterior valvae trunci pulmonalis
anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.summary: One of the three cup-shaped leaflets of the pulmonary valve. It lies at the front of the valve opening.
anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.location: At the base of the pulmonary trunk, where the right ventricular outflow tract ends.
function: Opens during ventricular systole so blood leaves the right ventricle
Closes with its neighbors to prevent backflow into the right ventricle
blood: Mostly avascular; nourished by diffusion from blood in the heart chambers
anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.nerve: Cardiac plexus; the leaflets have few nerve endings
anterior-semilunar-leaflet-of-pulmonary-.clinical: Pulmonary stenosis narrows the valve and strains the right ventricle. Its closure forms the pulmonic part of the second heart sound.

anterior-vein-of-left-lung.name: Anterior Vein of Left Lung
anterior-vein-of-left-lung.latin: Vena anterior lobi superioris pulmonis sinistri
anterior-vein-of-left-lung.summary: A tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein. It drains the anterior segment of the left upper lobe.
drains: Anterior segment of the left upper lobe
anterior-vein-of-left-lung.course: Runs between lung segments in the connective tissue septa, not beside the bronchi, and joins the apicoposterior and lingular veins.
anterior-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Segmental resection must preserve or divide intersegmental veins carefully. Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

anterior-vein-of-right-lung.name: Anterior Vein of Right Lung
anterior-vein-of-right-lung.latin: Vena anterior lobi superioris pulmonis dextri
anterior-vein-of-right-lung.summary: A tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein. It drains the anterior segment of the right upper lobe.
drains: Anterior segment of the right upper lobe
anterior-vein-of-right-lung.course: Runs in the septa between segments and joins the apical and posterior veins, then the middle lobe vein, to form the right superior pulmonary vein.
anterior-vein-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. Injury during lobectomy causes serious bleeding.

aortic-arch.name: Aortic Arch
aortic-arch.summary: The curved part of the aorta between the ascending and descending aorta. It gives off the arteries to the head, neck, and arms.
aortic-arch.from: Ascending aorta, behind the manubrium at about the level of the sternal angle
aortic-arch.course: Arches up, back, and to the left over the root of the left lung and left main bronchus. It ends at T4 to T5 as the descending aorta.
supplies: Head, neck, and both upper limbs through its three branches
aortic-arch.clinical: Coarctation usually occurs near the ligamentum arteriosum. An aneurysm can stretch the left recurrent laryngeal nerve and cause hoarseness.

apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.name: Apical Segmental Artery of Left Lung
apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.parent: Superior lobar artery of left lung
apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery to segment S1. It carries deoxygenated blood to the apical segment of the left upper lobe.
apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.from: Superior lobar branches of the left pulmonary artery
apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the apical segment of the left upper lobe
apical-segmental-artery-of-left-lung.clinical: Tuberculosis often settles in the apical segments. On the left, the apical and posterior segments are commonly fused as an apicoposterior segment.

apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.name: Apical Segmental Artery of Right Lung
apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.parent: Superior lobar artery of right lung
apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery to segment S1. It carries deoxygenated blood to the apical segment of the right upper lobe.
apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.from: Superior (anterior) trunk of the right pulmonary artery
apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the apical segment of the right upper lobe
apical-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: Reactivated tuberculosis often settles in the apical segments. A pulmonary embolus can also block this artery.

apical-vein-of-right-lung.name: Apical Vein of Right Lung
apical-vein-of-right-lung.latin: Vena apicalis lobi superioris pulmonis dextri
apical-vein-of-right-lung.summary: A tributary of the right superior pulmonary vein. It drains the apical segment of the right upper lobe.
drains: Apical segment of the right upper lobe
apical-vein-of-right-lung.course: Runs in the septa between lung segments toward the hilum and joins the anterior and posterior veins.
apical-vein-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. They are divided during upper lobectomy.

apicoposterior-vein-of-left-lung.name: Apicoposterior Vein of Left Lung
apicoposterior-vein-of-left-lung.latin: Vena apicoposterior lobi superioris pulmonis sinistri
apicoposterior-vein-of-left-lung.summary: A tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein. It drains the apical and posterior segments of the left upper lobe.
drains: Apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe
apicoposterior-vein-of-left-lung.course: Runs in the septa between segments toward the hilum and joins the anterior and lingular veins.
apicoposterior-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. Surgeons divide them carefully during left upper lobectomy.

ascending-aorta.name: Ascending Aorta
ascending-aorta.summary: The first part of the aorta, about 5 cm long. It begins at the aortic valve and lies inside the pericardium.
ascending-aorta.from: Left ventricle, through the aortic valve
ascending-aorta.course: Rises obliquely up and to the right behind the sternum and ends at the sternal angle, where it becomes the aortic arch.
supplies: Heart muscle through the coronary arteries
ascending-aorta.clinical: Aneurysm or dissection here (Stanford type A) is a surgical emergency. Aortic regurgitation can stretch the root.

azygos-vein.name: Azygos Vein
azygos-vein.summary: The main vein of the right posterior thoracic wall. It drains the posterior chest wall and connects the inferior and superior venae cavae.
drains: Esophageal, bronchial, pericardial, and mediastinal veins
azygos-vein.into: Superior vena cava, at about T4
azygos-vein.course: Begins at the ascending lumbar and right subcostal veins, passes through the aortic hiatus, and ascends right of the vertebrae. It arches over the right lung root.
azygos-vein.clinical: It provides a collateral route if the inferior or superior vena cava is blocked. An enlarged azygos arch may show on chest imaging.

bifurcation-of-pulmonary-trunk.name: Bifurcation of Pulmonary Trunk
bifurcation-of-pulmonary-trunk.summary: The point where the pulmonary trunk divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries. It lies below the aortic arch.
bifurcation-of-pulmonary-trunk.from: Pulmonary trunk, at about T5 to T6 (level of the sternal angle)
bifurcation-of-pulmonary-trunk.course: Sits in the concavity of the aortic arch, just left of the midline. The ligamentum arteriosum attaches near it.
supplies: Both lungs through the right and left pulmonary arteries
bifurcation-of-pulmonary-trunk.clinical: A large saddle pulmonary embolus lodges here and can cause sudden collapse.

brachiocephalic-trunk.name: Brachiocephalic Trunk
brachiocephalic-trunk.summary: The first and largest branch of the aortic arch. It supplies the right arm and the right side of the head and neck.
brachiocephalic-trunk.course: Ascends up and to the right in front of the trachea. It divides behind the right sternoclavicular joint.
branches: Thyroid ima artery (present in a minority of people)
supplies: Right side of the head and neck
brachiocephalic-trunk.clinical: It crosses the trachea and can be eroded by a low tracheostomy tube. A thyroid ima artery can bleed during surgery.

circumflex-artery-of-heart.name: Circumflex Artery
circumflex-artery-of-heart.summary: The smaller terminal branch of the left coronary artery. It wraps around the left side of the heart in the coronary sulcus.
circumflex-artery-of-heart.from: Left coronary artery, behind the pulmonary trunk
circumflex-artery-of-heart.course: Runs in the coronary sulcus to the left, around the left border, and onto the back of the heart.
supplies: Lateral and posterior wall of the left ventricle
circumflex-artery-of-heart.location: Left coronary sulcus between the left atrium and left ventricle
function: Delivers oxygenated blood to the left atrium and the side and back of the left ventricle
blood: Arterial wall nourished by its own lumen and vasa vasorum
circumflex-artery-of-heart.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
circumflex-artery-of-heart.clinical: Blockage causes a lateral wall infarct. In about 10 to 15 percent of people it gives the posterior interventricular artery (left dominance).

coronary-sinus.name: Coronary Sinus
coronary-sinus.summary: The main vein of the heart. It collects most venous blood from the heart wall and opens into the right atrium.
drains: Posterior vein of the left ventricle
Oblique vein of the left atrium
coronary-sinus.into: Right atrium, between the inferior vena cava opening and the tricuspid valve
coronary-sinus.course: Lies in the posterior part of the coronary sulcus, a continuation of the great cardiac vein. A small valve guards its opening.
coronary-sinus.clinical: Cardiac resynchronization pacing leads are placed through the coronary sinus. Surgeons can also give retrograde cardioplegia through it.

costocervical-trunk.name: Costocervical Trunk
costocervical-trunk.summary: A short branch of the subclavian artery in the root of the neck. It divides into the deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries.
costocervical-trunk.from: Subclavian artery: second part (behind scalenus anterior) on the right, first part on the left
costocervical-trunk.course: Passes up and back over the dome of the pleura to the neck of the first rib, then divides.
supplies: Deep muscles of the back of the neck
costocervical-trunk.clinical: It forms collateral links between the subclavian artery and the posterior intercostal and occipital arteries.

deep-branch-of-transverse-cervical-arter.name: Deep Branch of Transverse Cervical Artery
deep-branch-of-transverse-cervical-arter.summary: The branch that runs down the medial border of the scapula. It is the same vessel as the dorsal scapular artery when that artery arises from the transverse cervical artery.
deep-branch-of-transverse-cervical-arter.from: Transverse cervical artery, from the thyrocervical trunk
deep-branch-of-transverse-cervical-arter.course: Passes deep to levator scapulae and the rhomboids, then descends along the medial border of the scapula.
branches: Muscular branches to the rhomboids, levator scapulae, and trapezius
deep-branch-of-transverse-cervical-arter.clinical: It joins the scapular anastomosis. This route keeps blood flowing to the arm if the axillary artery is blocked.

deep-cervical-artery.name: Deep Cervical Artery
deep-cervical-artery.summary: A branch of the costocervical trunk that supplies the deep muscles at the back of the neck.
deep-cervical-artery.course: Passes back between the transverse process of C7 and the neck of the first rib, then ascends between semispinalis capitis and semispinalis cervicis.
branches: Branches that join the occipital artery
deep-cervical-artery.clinical: It anastomoses with the descending branch of the occipital artery, linking the subclavian and external carotid systems.

first-posterior-intercostal-artery.name: First Posterior Intercostal Artery
first-posterior-intercostal-artery.summary: The artery of the first intercostal space. It arises from the supreme intercostal artery, not from the aorta.
first-posterior-intercostal-artery.from: Supreme intercostal artery, from the costocervical trunk
first-posterior-intercostal-artery.course: Descends in front of the neck of the first rib and runs forward in the first intercostal space.
branches: Dorsal branch to the back and spinal canal
Anterior connection to the internal thoracic artery
supplies: Muscles and skin of the first intercostal space
first-posterior-intercostal-artery.clinical: It anastomoses with the anterior intercostal artery from the internal thoracic artery, forming a loop around the thoracic wall.

great-cardiac-vein.name: Great Cardiac Vein
great-cardiac-vein.summary: The main vein on the front of the heart. It travels beside the anterior interventricular artery and becomes the coronary sinus.
drains: Anterior part of the interventricular septum
great-cardiac-vein.course: Begins near the apex, ascends in the anterior interventricular groove, then turns left in the coronary sulcus to the back of the heart.
great-cardiac-vein.clinical: It runs beside the left anterior descending artery and can serve as an access route for left ventricular pacing leads.

hemi-azygos-vein.name: Hemi-azygos Vein
hemi-azygos-vein.summary: The left-sided partner of the azygos vein. It drains the lower left posterior intercostal spaces.
hemi-azygos-vein.into: Azygos vein, at about T8 to T9
hemi-azygos-vein.course: Ascends on the left of the lower thoracic vertebrae, then crosses the midline behind the aorta, thoracic duct, and esophagus.
hemi-azygos-vein.clinical: It provides a collateral route between the lower body and the superior vena cava if the inferior vena cava is blocked.

inferior-basal-vein-of-left-lung.name: Inferior Basal Vein of Left Lung
inferior-basal-vein-of-left-lung.summary: A basal vein of the left lower lobe. It joins the superior basal vein to form the common basal vein.
drains: Lower part of the basal segments of the left lower lobe
inferior-basal-vein-of-left-lung.into: Common basal vein, then the left inferior pulmonary vein
inferior-basal-vein-of-left-lung.course: Runs in the septa between basal segments toward the hilum.
inferior-basal-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. Left lower lobectomy divides the inferior pulmonary vein at the hilum.

inferior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.name: Inferior Basal Vein of Right Lung
inferior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.summary: A basal vein of the right lower lobe. It joins the superior basal vein to form the common basal vein.
drains: Lower part of the basal segments of the right lower lobe
inferior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.into: Common basal vein, then the right inferior pulmonary vein
inferior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.course: Runs in the septa between basal segments toward the hilum.
inferior-basal-vein-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. The right inferior pulmonary vein lies lowest in the hilum and is divided in lower lobectomy.

inferior-leaflet-of-right-atrioventricul.name: Inferior Leaflet of Right Atrioventricular Valve
inferior-leaflet-of-right-atrioventricul.summary: One of the three leaflets of the tricuspid valve. It lies along the inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the right ventricle and is also called the posterior leaflet.
inferior-leaflet-of-right-atrioventricul.location: Attached to the tricuspid annulus along the inferior wall of the right ventricle.
function: Closes the valve during ventricular systole with the other two leaflets
Prevents blood flowing back into the right atrium
blood: Mostly avascular; nourished by diffusion from blood in the heart chambers
inferior-leaflet-of-right-atrioventricul.nerve: Cardiac plexus; the leaflets have few nerve endings
inferior-leaflet-of-right-atrioventricul.clinical: Chordae tendineae to this leaflet arise from the anterior and inferior papillary muscles. Right ventricular dilation causes tricuspid regurgitation.

inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.name: Inferior Lingular Artery of Left Lung
inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.parent: Superior lobar artery of left lung
inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery to the inferior lingular segment (S5). It supplies the lower part of the lingula.
inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.from: Lingular branch of the superior lobar artery of the left pulmonary artery
inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the inferior lingular segment of the left upper lobe
inferior-lingular-artery-of-left-lung.clinical: The lingula corresponds to the right middle lobe. The lingula lies against the heart and is a common site of chronic infection, bronchiectasis, and atelectasis.

inferior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.name: Inferior Lingular Vein of Left Lung
inferior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.summary: A tributary of the left superior pulmonary vein. It drains the inferior part of the lingula of the left upper lobe.
drains: Inferior lingular segment of the left upper lobe
inferior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.into: Left superior pulmonary vein, usually joining the superior lingular vein first
inferior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.course: Runs in the septum between lingular segments toward the hilum.
inferior-lingular-vein-of-left-lung.clinical: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. The lingula lies against the heart and is prone to infection.

inferior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.name: Inferior Lobar Artery of Right Lung
inferior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.summary: The lower continuation of the right interlobar artery. It supplies the right lower lobe.
inferior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.from: Interlobar part of the right pulmonary artery, after the middle lobar branch
inferior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.course: Descends behind the bronchus intermedius toward the lower lobe and divides into the superior segmental artery and the basal trunk.
branches: Basal trunk, giving the medial, anterior, lateral, and posterior basal arteries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the right lower lobe
inferior-lobar-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: Pulmonary emboli often lodge in the lower lobe arteries because they receive the most blood flow.

inferior-papillary-muscle-of-left-ventri.name: Inferior Papillary Muscle of Left Ventricle
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-left-ventri.summary: The posterior (inferior) of the two papillary muscles of the left ventricle. It anchors the mitral valve.
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-left-ventri.location: Rises from the inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the left ventricle near the septum.
function: Holds the adjacent halves of both mitral leaflets closed during systole through chordae tendineae
Prevents mitral prolapse into the left atrium
blood: Posterior interventricular artery (usually a single supply)
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-left-ventri.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-left-ventri.clinical: A single blood supply makes it prone to ischemia and rupture after inferior myocardial infarction, causing acute mitral regurgitation.

inferior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.name: Inferior Papillary Muscle of Right Ventricle
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.summary: A small papillary muscle on the inferior wall of the right ventricle. It is often split into several heads.
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.location: Rises from the inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the right ventricle.
function: Anchors the posterior (inferior) and septal tricuspid leaflets through chordae tendineae
Helps keep the valve closed during systole
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
inferior-papillary-muscle-of-right-ventr.clinical: Dysfunction after an inferior infarct can cause tricuspid regurgitation.

inferior-phrenic-artery.name: Inferior Phrenic Artery
inferior-phrenic-artery.summary: The paired artery to the underside of the diaphragm. It usually arises from the abdominal aorta just above the celiac trunk.
inferior-phrenic-artery.from: Abdominal aorta just above the celiac trunk (sometimes the celiac trunk)
inferior-phrenic-artery.course: Ascends on the crus of the diaphragm and divides into branches on its inferior surface.
branches: Branches to the esophagus and inferior vena cava
inferior-phrenic-artery.clinical: It can become an extra blood supply to liver tumors, so liver embolization procedures may need to include it.

inferior-thyroid-artery.name: Inferior Thyroid Artery
inferior-thyroid-artery.summary: A branch of the thyrocervical trunk. It supplies the thyroid gland, the parathyroid glands, and nearby organs.
inferior-thyroid-artery.from: Thyrocervical trunk, from the first part of the subclavian artery
inferior-thyroid-artery.course: Ascends on scalenus anterior, then curves medially behind the carotid sheath at about C6 to reach the back of the thyroid gland.
inferior-thyroid-artery.clinical: The recurrent laryngeal nerve crosses it, so surgeons tie the artery close to the gland during thyroidectomy.

inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.name: Inferior Vein of Left Ventricle
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.summary: A small cardiac vein on the diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle. It drains into the coronary sinus.
drains: Inferior (diaphragmatic) surface of the left ventricle
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.into: Coronary sinus (or the great cardiac vein)
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.course: Runs on the inferior wall of the left ventricle toward the coronary sinus. It is also called the posterior vein of the left ventricle.
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.location: Inferior surface of the left ventricle
function: Returns deoxygenated blood from the inferior wall of the left ventricle to the coronary sinus
blood: Thin venous wall nourished mainly by blood in its lumen
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle.clinical: It is a possible target vein for left ventricular pacing leads.

inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.name: Posterior Vein of Left Ventricle
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.summary: A small cardiac vein on the back of the left ventricle. It drains into the coronary sinus.
drains: Diaphragmatic surface of the left ventricle
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.into: Coronary sinus, near the middle cardiac vein
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.course: Runs on the inferior wall of the left ventricle toward the coronary sinus.
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.location: Inferior surface of the left ventricle
function: Returns deoxygenated blood from the inferior wall of the left ventricle to the coronary sinus
blood: Thin venous wall nourished mainly by blood in its lumen
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.nerve: Cardiac plexus (sympathetic fibers from T1 to T4 and vagal fibers)
inferior-vein-of-left-ventricle-posterio.clinical: It is a possible target vein for left ventricular pacing leads.

inferior-vena-cava-th.name: Inferior Vena Cava (Thoracic Part)
inferior-vena-cava-th.summary: The short thoracic part of the inferior vena cava. It runs from the diaphragm to the right atrium.
drains: Blood from the lower limbs, pelvis, abdomen, and inferior phrenic veins
inferior-vena-cava-th.course: Pierces the central tendon of the diaphragm at T8, and after about 2 cm enters the lower part of the right atrium.
inferior-vena-cava-th.clinical: Most of its length is abdominal. Tumor or clot extending up this vein can reach the right atrium.

internal-thoracic-artery.name: Internal Thoracic Artery
internal-thoracic-artery.summary: A branch of the subclavian artery that descends just behind the costal cartilages beside the sternum. It supplies the front of the chest wall.
internal-thoracic-artery.from: Subclavian artery, first part, opposite the thyrocervical trunk
internal-thoracic-artery.course: Descends behind the clavicle and first costal cartilage, about 1 cm from the sternal edge. It ends in the 6th intercostal space.
internal-thoracic-artery.clinical: The left internal thoracic artery is the standard graft for bypass of the left anterior descending artery.

internal-thoracic-veins.name: Internal Thoracic Veins
internal-thoracic-veins.summary: Paired veins that accompany the internal thoracic artery. They drain the front of the chest wall.
internal-thoracic-veins.into: Brachiocephalic vein on the same side
internal-thoracic-veins.course: Usually two veins below and one above the third costal cartilage. They run beside the sternum and end behind the first costal cartilage.
internal-thoracic-veins.clinical: They carry breast venous blood and are a route for spread of breast cancer to the mediastinum.

lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.name: Lateral Basal Segmental Artery of Left Lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.latin: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis sinistri
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.parent: Inferior lobar artery of left lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.summary: A segmental branch of the left pulmonary artery to segment S9. It carries deoxygenated blood to the lateral basal segment of the left lower lobe.
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.from: Basal trunk of the inferior lobar artery of the left lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the lateral basal segment of the left lower lobe
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-left-l.clinical: Pulmonary embolism can block it and cause a wedge-shaped infarct. Basal segments are common sites of atelectasis after surgery.

lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.name: Lateral Basal Segmental Artery of Right Lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.latin: Arteria segmentalis basalis lateralis pulmonis dextri
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.parent: Inferior lobar artery of right lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.summary: A segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery to segment S9. It carries deoxygenated blood to the lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe.
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.from: Basal trunk of the inferior lobar artery of the right lung
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe
lateral-basal-segmental-artery-of-right-.clinical: Pulmonary embolism can block it and cause a wedge-shaped infarct. Basal segments are common sites of atelectasis after surgery.

lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.name: Lateral Segmental Artery of Right Lung
lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.parent: Middle lobar artery of right lung
lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.summary: A segmental branch of the right pulmonary artery to segment S4. It carries deoxygenated blood to the lateral segment of the right middle lobe.
lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.from: Middle lobar artery of the right pulmonary artery
lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.course: Runs beside the segmental bronchus, usually on its lateral or posterior side, into the bronchopulmonary segment.
branches: Subsegmental branches that end in the pulmonary capillaries
supplies: Deoxygenated blood to the lateral segment of the right middle lobe
lateral-segmental-artery-of-right-lung.clinical: The narrow middle lobe bronchus is easily compressed by nodes, causing middle lobe syndrome with collapse of both segments.
